newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude flat on ACCESS, technicals dominate.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude flat on ACCESS, technicals dominate.

text.p: U.S. crude oil futures drifted sideways in early after-hours trade, on thin volume as many traders observed the Yom Kippur holiday or watched key technical levels.

Traders said if NYMEX crude for November delivery broke Monday's support of $22.85 a barrel on Tuesday, they would watch for more declines to $22.20 -- a level where buyers would scramble to pick it up, with supplies seen low and demand up.
But if the contract exceeded $23.50/23.55 it could test the high of $24.64 reached on September 13 on Middle East tensions.
November crude traded at $23.37 a barrel by 0030 GMT on ACCESS, unchanged from Monday's settle, with around 375 lots exchanged. Around 174 contracts traded in December.
October heating oil and gasolines were thinly traded, with front-month "heat" up seven points to 67.55 cents a gallon after rising a slight 0.06 cent in day trade. Around 50 lots changed hands.
October unleaded rose 0.43 cent to 60.50 a gallon, trimming its daytime loss of 1.02 cents.
